newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa inquiry rejects return of mercury waste.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa inquiry rejects return of mercury waste.

text.p: A South African commission of inquiry on Tuesday rejected a suggestion that stocks of hazardous mercury waste be returned to the countries of origin, including the United States, Italy, Indonesia and Brazil.

The commission was appointed by the government to probe the accumulation of about 3,300 tonnes of mercury waste at a recycling plant owned by Thor Chemicals, a subsidiary of a British company of the same name, in KwaZulu-Natal province.

The commission's report released on Tuesday said the waste, some of it imported from the United States, Brazil, Indonesia, the Gulf and Italy, could not be recycled as planned because a special plant built by Thor had failed to work properly.

Environmental groups proposed returning the imported portion to the countries of origin, but the commission said this was not feasible because of international conventions against such shipments, the dangers of transport and the absence of indications from the countries that they would accept the waste.
The commission said the best disposal option appeared to be incineration.
Commission chairman Dennis Davis told reporters that urgent steps should be taken to neutralise the waste, which began arriving at the plant in the early 1980s.
"The longer we mess around, the more hazardous it becomes," he said.
In the late 1980s South African scientists found high levels of mercury in rivers below the Thor plant.
Last month Thor's British parent company reached a 9.4 million rand ($2.1 million) settlement with 20 workers at the South African plant who said they had suffered mercury poisoning.
